Thanks Daniel — included below is a compact "Stopsign Playbook" we discussed. I’m attaching a proposed MAP workbook (OrthoSure_MAP_v1.xlsx) with the sprint-by-sprint activities and a separate test-case doc (stopsign-test-cases.md).

High level stopsign (one-pager):
- Sprint goal (quantitative): e.g., 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms on representative requests AND token-level concordance >= 92% on labeled prompt set.
- Safety/QA pass: no unresolved P0 data-handling issues; audit log captured for sample session.
- Integration checklist: API auth, VPC egress, and telemetry ingest verified by integration runbook.
- Business acceptance: 3 cross-functional stakeholders sign off (Engineering, Product, RegOps) or documented objections.

If any of the above fails at the sprint review:
- Fail-fast options: remediate in the next 1-week hotfix sprint OR pause rollout and transition to fallback model (R7-lite) with agreed ramp-down.
- Credit/compensation trigger: if remediation window exceeds 14 calendar days, we escalate to commercial remedy conversation (per draft MAP).

Proposed next steps:
1) Our engineer (Connor) will run the initial smoke tests against your dev cluster by Friday.
2) Ben will prepare the concordance harness and share sample results.
3) Legal: please flag any problematic language in the timeline/credit triggers in the MAP workbook.

I’ve kept each signal operational (measurable) so you can plug them into a pass/fail column. If you want, we can convert the stopsign into a single-sheet sign-off checklist for your Execs.

Kimberly Park
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Stopsign: evaluation playbook, gate tests, and go/no-go choreography (OrthoSure pilot)

Quick update from the infra side: I ran the smoke run against OrthoSure dev (token-limited sample) and saw two notable items:
- Latency: median looks good (270ms) but tail spikes to ~520ms on 1% of traces when payloads include long clinical notes. I’m attaching the run log.
- Telemetry: our trace IDs aren’t being propagated from your proxy in ~8% of calls; that blocks accurate per-request cost attribution.

Action plan I propose for the sprint:
A) Tail latency: enable prefix-KV caching for clinical-note-heavy flows (we can toggle at runtime). Connor will own a 48-hour pilot and report results.
B) Trace propagation: Ben will send a small header shim (3 lines) for your proxy to set trace-id; deploy in dev by EOD Friday.

These touchpoints map to the Stopsign items: tail latency is a quantitative metric; trace propagation is an integration checklist item. If either remains unresolved at sprint review, the Stopsign flags a remediation sprint.

Will push logs and a sample concordance run to the Drive link.

--Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood

Attaching the concordance harness result (summary below). Short summary: on the 120-sample labeled set the model variant passed the 92% threshold (observed 93.5% concordance) but two edge-case prompts (free-text forms with OCR artifacts) dropped below 80%.

Proposal: add an edge-case acceptance test to the Stopsign that requires a follow-up remediation plan for OCR-heavy inputs. That would change the business-acceptance item from "3 stakeholders sign off" to "3 stakeholders sign off + OCR edge-case mitigation plan documented".

I’ll populate the stopsign-test-cases.md with the failing samples and suggested mitigations.

Ben
Principal ML Engineer, Redwood
